name: Four Forces
tagline: Lift · Drag · Thrust · Weight — the fundamentals of flight

rows.label: Lift
rows.info: Aerodynamic force produced perpendicular to the relative wind — primarily generated by the wings

rows.label: Drag
rows.info: Aerodynamic force acting parallel to and in the same direction as the relative wind — opposes flight path

rows.label: Thrust
rows.info: Forward force produced by the powerplant/propeller — overcomes drag and accelerates the aircraft

rows.label: Weight
rows.info: Combined load of the aircraft, crew, fuel, and cargo acting downward through the center of gravity (CG)

rows.label: Straight-and-level (unaccelerated)
rows.info: Lift = Weight · Thrust = Drag — no net force in any direction

rows.label: Climb
rows.info: Thrust must overcome Drag plus a rearward component of Weight — Lift is slightly less than Weight

rows.label: Descent
rows.info: A component of Weight acts forward along the flight path — less thrust required than level flight

rows.label: Turn
rows.info: Lift is divided into vertical component (supports weight) and horizontal component (centripetal force) — total lift must increase

sections.title: Center of Pressure & Center of Gravity

rows.label: Center of Pressure (CP)
rows.info: Point on the chord line through which the resultant aerodynamic force acts — moves forward as AOA increases

rows.label: Center of Gravity (CG)
rows.info: Point about which the aircraft would balance — must remain within approved limits for controllability

rows.label: CG aft of limits
rows.info: Unstable — nose tends to pitch up, harder to recover from stalls

rows.label: CG forward of limits
rows.info: Very stable but reduced pitch authority — may not rotate or flare adequately

name: Lift & AOA
tagline: Bernoulli, Newton, critical AOA, and the lift equation

rows.label: Definition
rows.info: Angle between the chord line of the wing and the relative wind — NOT pitch attitude

rows.label: Relative wind
rows.info: Direction of airflow relative to the aircraft — always opposite and parallel to the flight path

rows.label: Increasing AOA
rows.info: Increases lift (up to critical AOA) and induced drag — CL increases

rows.label: Critical AOA
rows.info: AOA at which the wing stalls — airflow separates from upper surface — typically 15–18° depending on airfoil

rows.label: AOA is independent of airspeed
rows.info: A wing can stall at any airspeed — only the critical AOA determines the stall, not a specific speed

rows.label: Bernoulli's Principle
rows.info: Increased airflow velocity over the curved upper surface creates lower pressure — pressure differential generates lift upward

rows.label: Newton's Third Law
rows.info: Wing deflects airflow downward — equal and opposite reaction produces upward lift force

rows.label: Both theories apply
rows.info: Actual lift results from both pressure differential and deflection of airflow — neither alone fully explains it

rows.label: Camber
rows.info: Curvature of the airfoil — greater camber produces more lift at a given AOA but also more drag

rows.label: CL (lift coefficient)
rows.info: Varies with AOA and airfoil shape — increases to CLmax at critical AOA, then drops sharply

rows.label: ρ (air density)
rows.info: Decreases with altitude, high temperature, and high humidity — less dense air = less lift at same speed

rows.label: V² (velocity squared)
rows.info: Doubling airspeed quadruples lift — speed has the greatest effect on lift

rows.label: S (wing area)
rows.info: Larger wing area produces more lift — some aircraft use flaps to increase effective wing area

rows.label: Flaps (general)
rows.info: Increase camber and/or wing area — increase both lift and drag — lower stall speed

rows.label: Plain / split flaps
rows.info: Simple deflection — increase drag significantly, moderate lift increase

rows.label: Slotted flaps
rows.info: Slot energizes boundary layer — better lift-to-drag ratio — most common on GA aircraft

rows.label: Fowler flaps
rows.info: Extend rearward and down — large lift increase with moderate drag — used on larger aircraft

rows.label: Effect on stall speed
rows.info: Flaps lower stall speed by allowing level flight at a lower airspeed — but stall AOA is unchanged

name: Drag
tagline: Parasite + Induced = Total drag · L/Dmax = best glide

rows.label: Form drag
rows.info: Pressure difference fore-and-aft of the aircraft — reduced by streamlining (teardrop shapes)

rows.label: Skin friction drag
rows.info: Friction of air moving along the aircraft surface — reduced by smooth surfaces and laminar airfoils

rows.label: Interference drag
rows.info: Turbulence at junctions of structural components (wing-fuselage, etc.) — reduced by fairings and fillets

rows.label: Speed relationship
rows.info: Parasite drag increases with the square of airspeed — doubling speed quadruples parasite drag

rows.label: Cause
rows.info: By-product of lift — high-pressure air below wing spills around wingtip to low-pressure side, creating vortices

rows.label: Wingtip vortices
rows.info: Counter-rotating spirals of air trailing from each wingtip — source of wake turbulence

rows.label: Speed relationship
rows.info: Induced drag decreases with the square of airspeed — slower speed = higher AOA = more induced drag

rows.label: High aspect ratio
rows.info: Long, narrow wings have less induced drag — gliders use high-aspect-ratio wings for efficiency

rows.label: Total drag
rows.info: Sum of parasite and induced drag — has a U-shaped curve vs. airspeed with a minimum point

rows.label: L/Dmax speed
rows.info: Airspeed where total drag is minimized and lift-to-drag ratio is greatest — equals best glide speed (Vbg)

rows.label: Flying slower than L/Dmax
rows.info: Induced drag dominates — 'back side of the power curve' — more power needed to fly slower

rows.label: Flying faster than L/Dmax
rows.info: Parasite drag dominates — also requires more power but aircraft is on the 'front side' of power curve

name: Stability
tagline: Three axes, static vs dynamic, positive/neutral/negative

rows.label: Longitudinal axis
rows.info: Runs nose-to-tail — roll motion — controlled by ailerons

rows.label: Lateral axis
rows.info: Runs wingtip-to-wingtip — pitch motion — controlled by elevator (or stabilator)

rows.label: Vertical axis
rows.info: Runs top-to-bottom — yaw motion — controlled by rudder

rows.label: All axes intersect at CG
rows.info: Every rotation is about the center of gravity — CG position affects handling significantly

rows.label: Positive static stability
rows.info: Initial tendency to return to original attitude after a displacement — desirable in all axes

rows.label: Neutral static stability
rows.info: No tendency to return or diverge after displacement — remains in displaced attitude

rows.label: Negative static stability
rows.info: Initial tendency to move further away from original attitude — dangerous, found in some aerobatic aircraft

rows.label: Dynamic stability
rows.info: Describes the motion over time after displacement — positive dynamic = oscillations diminish; negative = oscillations grow

rows.label: Primary factor
rows.info: CG location relative to the neutral point — forward CG increases longitudinal stability

rows.label: Horizontal stabilizer
rows.info: Set at a slight negative angle of incidence — creates downward tail force that pitches nose down if nose rises

rows.label: Forward CG
rows.info: More stable, higher stick forces, may reduce climb performance — requires more back pressure to rotate

rows.label: Aft CG
rows.info: Less stable, lighter stick forces, better climb — risk of pitch divergence and reduced stall recovery margin

rows.label: Dihedral
rows.info: Wings angled up from root — when one wing drops, that wing develops more lift, restoring wings-level — positive lateral stability

rows.label: Sweepback
rows.info: Wings swept aft — yawing motion changes effective span, creating restoring roll — also aids directional stability

rows.label: Keel effect
rows.info: Side area of fuselage above CG acts like a weather vane — aids directional (yaw) stability

rows.label: Dutch roll
rows.info: Coupled rolling-yawing oscillation — inadequate directional vs. lateral stability — yaw dampers address this in jets

name: Stalls & Spins
tagline: Critical AOA exceeded — stall at any airspeed, any attitude

rows.label: Stall definition
rows.info: Occurs when the wing exceeds its critical angle of attack — airflow separates from the upper surface and lift decreases abruptly

rows.label: Stall speed varies with weight
rows.info: Heavier aircraft stall at higher indicated airspeeds — VS1 and VS0 are published at max gross weight

rows.label: Stall speed varies with bank
rows.info: Increased bank raises load factor, which raises the stall speed — 60° bank = 2g = 1.41× stall speed increase

rows.label: Stall warning
rows.info: Stall warning horn activates 5–10 kt above stall — may also include buffeting as disturbed tail airflow arrives

rows.label: Imminent stall cues
rows.info: Mushy controls, nose-high attitude, high power setting, buffet, stall horn — recognize and act immediately

rows.label: Step 1 — reduce AOA
rows.info: Forward pressure on elevator — simultaneously apply full power to minimize altitude loss

rows.label: Step 2 — wings level
rows.info: Use coordinated rudder to stop any yaw/roll, then aileron to level wings after AOA is reduced

rows.label: Step 3 — climb
rows.info: Once airspeed is in the normal range, pitch to Vx or Vy and return to desired altitude

rows.label: Secondary stall
rows.info: Pulling back too aggressively during recovery re-exceeds critical AOA before adequate airspeed is regained

rows.label: Spin definition
rows.info: Aggravated stall that results in autorotation about the vertical axis — both wings are stalled, one more than the other

rows.label: Phases
rows.info: Entry (stall + yaw) → Incipient (1–2 turns, not fully developed) → Developed (steady autorotation) → Recovery

rows.label: Incipient spin
rows.info: Most recoverable phase — recovery is identical to upright stall recovery with opposite rudder

rows.label: PARE recovery (power off)
rows.info: Power idle · Ailerons neutral · Rudder full opposite to spin direction · Elevator briskly forward to break stall

rows.label: Pull out
rows.info: Once rotation stops, neutralize rudder and apply smooth back pressure to recover from dive — avoid secondary stall

name: Load Factors
tagline: G-loads, V-speeds, maneuvering speed, structural limits

rows.label: Definition
rows.info: Ratio of the aerodynamic force on the wings to the actual gross weight of the aircraft (n = L/W) — measured in 'g'

rows.label: Straight-and-level
rows.info: Load factor = 1.0g — lift equals weight

rows.label: Steep turn at 60° bank
rows.info: Load factor = 2.0g — wings must produce twice the lift to maintain altitude

rows.label: Stall speed increase
rows.info: Stall speed increases as the square root of load factor — at 2g, stall speed × 1.41

rows.label: 30° bank
rows.info: Load factor = 1.15g — stall speed increases ~7%

rows.label: 45° bank
rows.info: Load factor = 1.41g — stall speed increases ~19%

rows.label: 60° bank
rows.info: Load factor = 2.0g — stall speed increases 41%

rows.label: 75° bank
rows.info: Load factor = 3.86g — approaching normal category structural limit

rows.label: 90° bank (vertical)
rows.info: Theoretically infinite load factor — impossible to sustain altitude

rows.label: Va — Maneuvering speed
rows.info: Maximum speed for full control deflection — at or below Va, the wing stalls before exceeding structural limits · decreases with reduced weight

rows.label: Vno — Normal operating limit
rows.info: Top of green arc — do not exceed in turbulence

rows.label: Vne — Never-exceed speed
rows.info: Top of yellow arc — structural damage or flutter above this speed

rows.label: Vfe — Flap extension speed
rows.info: Maximum speed for extending flaps — top of white arc

rows.label: Vle / Vlo — Gear speeds
rows.info: Vle = max speed with gear extended; Vlo = max speed for gear operation (retractable aircraft)

name: Slow Flight
tagline: Minimum controllable airspeed — back side of the power curve

rows.label: Purpose
rows.info: Develop ability to recognize and control the aircraft at minimum airspeeds — simulates approach-to-landing conditions

rows.label: Back side of power curve
rows.info: Below L/Dmax speed — more power is required to fly slower — airspeed and power have an inverse relationship

rows.label: High pitch attitude
rows.info: Required to maintain altitude at slow speed — large AOA — close to stall AOA

rows.label: Sluggish controls
rows.info: Control surfaces less effective at low airspeeds — larger inputs required to produce the desired response

rows.label: Allowing airspeed to decrease too much
rows.info: May result in unintentional stall — maintain target airspeed with power adjustments

rows.label: Inadequate rudder
rows.info: P-factor and torque significant at low speed/high power — must use right rudder to maintain coordinated flight

rows.label: Fixating on instruments
rows.info: Maintain outside scan — use pitch attitude and power as primary control inputs, verify with instruments

rows.label: Abrupt recovery inputs
rows.info: Smoothly add full power and reduce pitch to Vy — abrupt inputs can aggravate into a stall

name: Steep Turns
tagline: ≥45° bank · load factor 1.41g · ACS ±100 ft, ±10 kt, ±5°

rows.label: Increased load factor
rows.info: At 45° bank, load factor is 1.41g — the aircraft effectively weighs 41% more and stall speed increases accordingly

rows.label: Overbanking tendency
rows.info: In turns steeper than ~35°, the outside wing travels faster, generates more lift, and tends to increase the bank

rows.label: More back pressure needed
rows.info: Must increase pitch to maintain altitude as bank steepens — back elevator compensates for reduced vertical lift component

rows.label: Power increase required
rows.info: Increased drag from higher AOA at steep bank requires additional power to maintain airspeed and altitude

rows.label: Altitude loss in turn
rows.info: Insufficient back pressure — add elevator while maintaining bank to correct

rows.label: Gaining altitude in turn
rows.info: Excessive back pressure — release elevator slightly while maintaining bank

rows.label: Airspeed decreasing
rows.info: Increase power — if airspeed drops significantly, consider rolling to shallower bank to recover

rows.label: Late rollout
rows.info: Anticipate rollout and begin slightly early — the rollout takes time and the aircraft continues to turn during it

rows.label: Uncoordinated flight
rows.info: Watch the ball — skidding (ball outside) or slipping (ball inside) adds stress and can lead to accelerated stall

name: Stall Maneuvers
tagline: Power-off & power-on stalls — ACS altitude loss minimized

rows.label: Configuration
rows.info: Slow to approach speed of 78kts, flaps 100%, throttle idle — simulates base-to-final or final approach

rows.label: Entry
rows.info: Maintain approach airspeed, then slowly increase pitch to slow below approach speed — hold increasing back pressure until stall break

rows.label: Stall recognition
rows.info: Stall horn, mushy controls, nose-high attitude, buffet — full stall when nose breaks or uncontrolled pitch/roll

rows.label: Recovery
rows.info: Upset, push, roll, thrust, stabilize. Positive rate, pitch 85, clean, climb at Vy

rows.label: Configuration
rows.info: Approach speed of 78kts, flaps 50%, then apply takeoff/full power — simulates takeoff initial climb

rows.label: Entry
rows.info: At rotation speed with full power, pitch aggressively to simulate a too-steep initial climb — hold until stall break

rows.label: P-factor / torque effects
rows.info: Strong left-turning tendencies at high power/slow speed — right rudder required to maintain heading; may roll left at break

rows.label: Recovery
rows.info: Upset, push, roll, thrust, stabilize. Positive rate, pitch 85, clean, climb at Vy

name: Ground Reference
tagline: Rectangular course, S-turns, turns around a point — wind correction

rows.label: Purpose
rows.info: Simulates airport traffic pattern — develops ability to fly rectangular path while correcting for wind drift

rows.label: Entry
rows.info: Typically begin on downwind leg, 45° to field boundary, 600–1,000 ft AGL — plan crab angle before each turn

rows.label: Upwind leg
rows.info: Slight crab into wind to track parallel to the reference boundary — no crab needed if no crosswind component

rows.label: Downwind leg
rows.info: Wind behind — track parallel to boundary with crab toward field — fastest ground speed on this leg

rows.label: Corner turns
rows.info: Adjust bank angle based on ground speed — steeper bank upwind corners (slower), shallower downwind (faster)

rows.label: Purpose
rows.info: Develop ability to maintain a consistent radius on each half-circle while compensating for wind

rows.label: Entry
rows.info: Enter perpendicular to a straight road/line, on the downwind side — start with steepest bank

rows.label: Bank variation
rows.info: Bank is steepest when flying perpendicular downwind (fastest ground speed) and shallowest when perpendicular upwind (slowest)

rows.label: Wings level over road
rows.info: Must cross the reference road with wings level, perpendicular to road, and immediately begin turn in opposite direction

rows.label: Purpose
rows.info: Maintain constant radius around a ground reference — requires continuously varying bank to compensate for wind

rows.label: Entry
rows.info: Begin on the downwind side of the point — this requires the steepest bank to maintain radius against high ground speed

rows.label: Bank variation
rows.info: Steepest bank downwind (high ground speed), shallowest upwind (low ground speed) — bank constantly varies throughout

rows.label: Radius
rows.info: Select a prominent reference point and maintain approximately 600–1,000 ft radius — keep reference point at consistent wingtip position

rows.label: Inadequate wind correction
rows.info: Not applying enough crab or bank variation — results in irregular ground track drifting downwind

rows.label: Altitude variation
rows.info: Distraction from ground reference causes altitude deviations — maintain 600–1,000 ft AGL throughout

rows.label: Not rolling wings level on road
rows.info: S-turns require wings level exactly over the road — premature or late roll causes asymmetric semicircles

rows.label: Fixating on reference
rows.info: Must maintain normal scan for traffic while performing ground reference maneuvers
